title: Genealogies from Adam
summary: A long set of genealogies traces the human family from Adam through Noah's sons, Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac, Esau and Edom, and Israel's twelve sons. It gives special attention to Judah and David's line, then lists the tribes of Levi, Benjamin and others, including the priestly families, gatekeepers and singers, and ends with those who first returned from exile to live in Jerusalem. The chapters place David's story within the history of all Israel.

title: The Death of Saul
summary: The chronicler's account of Saul's end begins with the Philistines defeating Israel on Mount Gilboa, where Saul's sons Jonathan, Abinadab and Melchi-shua are killed. Wounded by archers, Saul asks his armor-bearer to kill him, and when he refuses, Saul falls on his sword. The Philistines display his armor in the temple of their gods and his head in the house of Dagon, and the men of Jabesh-gilead bury his bones. The chapter says Saul died for his unfaithfulness, including consulting a medium.

title: David Takes Jerusalem and Gathers His Warriors
summary: All Israel gathers at Hebron, anoints David king, and goes with him to take Jerusalem, where Joab wins command by being first to strike. The chapter lists David's mighty men, such as Jashobeam and Eleazar, and tells how three broke through to bring him water from Bethlehem, which he pours out to the LORD. Chapter 12 lists warriors from Benjamin, Gad, Judah, Manasseh and other tribes who joined him, and the tribes make him king at Hebron with a feast.

title: The Ark Brought to Jerusalem
summary: David consults the leaders and sets the ark on a new cart to bring it from Kirjath-jearim, but Uzza is struck dead when he reaches to steady it, and David leaves it at the house of Obed-edom. Hiram of Tyre sends cedar for David's house, and David defeats the Philistines. David then has the Levites carry the ark on their shoulders into Jerusalem with singers and instruments, and places it in a tent. The chapter ends with a psalm of thanks given to Asaph and his brothers.

title: God's Covenant with David and His Wars
summary: David wants to build a house for the ark, but God tells Nathan that David's son will build it and that God will establish David's house and throne forever. David prays in thanks. The next chapters record his wars: he defeats the Philistines, Moab, Syria and Edom, and the Ammonites after they humiliate his envoys, with Joab and Abishai leading the fighting at Rabbah. Several Philistine giants are killed in later battles, and tribute and plunder are dedicated to the LORD.

title: The Census and the Temple Site
summary: Satan stands against Israel and moves David to number the people; Joab objects, but the census counts 1,100,000 in Israel and 470,000 in Judah, totals that differ from those in 2 Samuel 24. God sends a plague, and David chooses three days of pestilence; when the angel stands over the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, David asks that the punishment fall on him. He buys the floor and builds an altar, and the plague stops. David then gathers materials and charges Solomon to build the temple.

title: Organizing the Levites, Priests and Officers
summary: Old David makes his son Solomon king and organizes the Levites by family, from age twenty, for temple service. The priests are divided into twenty-four courses by lot, the singers and musicians into twenty-four groups, and the gatekeepers into courses. David also appoints treasurers, army divisions of 24,000 for each month, tribal leaders, and royal officials. The text records that David did not number those under twenty, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as many as the stars.

title: David's Last Charge and Death
summary: David assembles Israel's leaders, tells them God chose Solomon to build the temple, and gives Solomon the plans for the house and its furnishings. He tells Solomon to serve God with a whole heart and be strong. David and the leaders give gold, silver and precious stones, and David blesses the LORD in a prayer. Solomon is made king a second time and anointed, and David dies full of days, riches and honor after forty years as king.
